In one embodiment, the invention relates to a process for manufacturing an antenna substrate having a wiring line and an electrode, the process comprising the following operations: (1) applying, onto an insulating substrate, a photosensitive paste that includes a conductive material and a photosensitive organic component to form a coating film; (2-A) shaping the coating film by photolithography into a pattern for an antenna; (2-B) shaping the coating film into a pattern for a wiring line; (2-C) shaping the coating film into a pattern for an electrode; (3-A) curing the antenna pattern to form an antenna; (3-B) curing the wiring-line pattern to form a wiring line; and (3-C) curing the electrode pattern to form an electrode.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a method for accurately forming an antenna substrate by using a coating process. This method is particularly useful for producing fine conductive patterns, such as an antenna, a wiring line, and an electrode, on an insulating substrate with high precision.

In this method, a photosensitive paste is first prepared. The photosensitive paste contains a conductive material and a photosensitive organic component. The conductive material serves as the basis for forming the conductive portions of the antenna substrate, while the photosensitive organic component enables the paste to be patterned by photolithography.

Next, the photosensitive paste is applied onto an insulating substrate to form a coating film. This coating film functions as the starting layer from which the antenna, the wiring line, and the electrode will be formed. Because the layer is produced by a coating method, it can be formed efficiently and uniformly over the substrate surface.

The coating film is then subjected to photolithographic patterning. In this step, the film is exposed to light through a mask having predetermined pattern shapes corresponding to the desired antenna, wiring line, and electrode. After exposure and development, unnecessary portions of the coating film are removed, leaving patterned structures that match the intended conductive designs.

Finally, the patterned structures are cured. Through curing, the conductive material in the patterned paste is fixed and consolidated, and the organic component is hardened or otherwise treated to provide mechanical stability and electrical functionality. As a result, the final antenna, wiring line, and electrode are accurately formed on the insulating substrate.

Accordingly, the method enables precise formation of an antenna substrate using a coating process and photolithographic patterning, making it possible to produce conductive patterns with high accuracy and reliable performance.
outputs.L4:
The present invention relates to a method for manufacturing an antenna substrate in which an antenna pattern, wiring lines, and electrodes are integrally formed on an insulating substrate with high dimensional accuracy. More particularly, the invention provides a fabrication process that uses a coating technique and a photosensitive conductive paste to form conductive structures directly on a substrate, thereby enabling precise and reliable production of an integrated antenna substrate.

In the manufacturing method, an insulating substrate is first prepared as a base member. The insulating substrate may be formed of glass, ceramic, resin, or another electrically insulating material suitable for supporting an antenna circuit. A photosensitive conductive paste is then applied to a surface of the insulating substrate by a coating method such as screen coating, spin coating, roll coating, slit coating, or another suitable deposition technique. The photosensitive conductive paste contains conductive particles, a photosensitive resin component, and other additives as necessary, so that the coated layer can be patterned by exposure and development while also providing electrical conductivity after curing.

After the photosensitive conductive paste has been applied, the coated layer is subjected to photolithographic patterning. In this step, the coated layer is exposed to light through a photomask having a predetermined pattern corresponding to an antenna, wiring lines, and electrodes. The exposed layer is then developed to remove unnecessary portions of the paste, thereby leaving a patterned conductive paste layer on the insulating substrate. Through this process, the antenna pattern, the wiring line pattern, and the electrode pattern can be formed at desired positions with high precision.

The patterned conductive paste is subsequently cured. The curing process may include heating, baking, firing, ultraviolet curing, or a combination of such treatments depending on the composition of the photosensitive conductive paste and the material of the insulating substrate. By curing the patterned layer, the conductive particles are fixed and electrically connected, and the antenna, wiring lines, and electrodes are firmly bonded to the insulating substrate. As a result, a conductive pattern having sufficient mechanical strength, adhesion, and electrical conductivity is obtained.

According to this method, the antenna, wiring lines, and electrodes can be fabricated as integrated conductive features on the same insulating substrate without requiring separate attachment or complicated assembly steps. Since the conductive paste is patterned by photolithography after coating, fine patterns can be formed accurately and reproducibly. This makes it possible to manufacture an antenna substrate having a precise antenna configuration, reliable wiring connections, and accurately positioned electrodes.

The invention is particularly advantageous because it enables conductive features to be formed by a coating process while maintaining the pattern accuracy generally associated with photolithographic techniques. Therefore, the method improves manufacturing efficiency, reduces alignment errors, and enhances the reliability of the finished antenna substrate. The resulting integrated antenna substrate can be used in various electronic devices, communication modules, wireless tags, sensors, and other products requiring compact and accurately formed antenna structures.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style summary for an invention involving forming an antenna substrate with an antenna, wiring line, and electrode using a photosensitive conductive paste and photolithography.
counterfactuals.output:
## Summary

An embodiment of the invention provides a method of forming an antenna substrate including an antenna pattern, a wiring line, and an electrode on a base substrate by using a photosensitive conductive paste and a photolithographic process. The method may include applying a photosensitive conductive paste onto at least one surface of an insulating substrate, selectively exposing the photosensitive conductive paste to light through a photomask having a predetermined pattern corresponding to an antenna portion, a wiring-line portion, and an electrode portion, developing the exposed paste to remove an unneeded region, and curing or firing the remaining patterned conductive paste to form an integrated conductive pattern.

In one aspect, the antenna, the wiring line, and the electrode are formed from the same photosensitive conductive paste in a single patterning process. Accordingly, alignment errors between separately formed conductive components may be reduced, and manufacturing steps may be simplified. The resulting antenna substrate may exhibit improved dimensional accuracy, reduced production cost, and enhanced reliability.

In another aspect, the photosensitive conductive paste may include conductive particles, a photosensitive resin, a photopolymerization initiator, and a solvent. The conductive particles may include at least one of silver, copper, gold, nickel, aluminum, carbon, or an alloy or composite thereof. The paste may be configured to provide sufficient conductivity after curing or firing while maintaining photolithographic patternability before curing.

In certain embodiments, the antenna pattern may be formed as a coil, loop, spiral, meander, dipole, patch, or other antenna geometry suitable for radio-frequency communication. The wiring line may electrically connect the antenna pattern to the electrode, and the electrode may be configured for connection to an external circuit, semiconductor chip, module, terminal, or other electronic component.

In a further embodiment, the method enables fine-line formation of the antenna pattern and the wiring line without requiring etching of a metal foil or plating process. Because the conductive pattern is directly formed by exposure and development of the photosensitive conductive paste, material waste may be reduced and a flexible design change may be achieved by changing the photomask.

An antenna substrate according to an embodiment includes a base substrate and a patterned conductive layer disposed on the base substrate. The patterned conductive layer includes an antenna, a wiring line extending from the antenna, and an electrode connected to the wiring line, wherein the antenna, wiring line, and electrode are integrally formed from a cured photosensitive conductive paste. The antenna substrate may be used in, for example, an RFID tag, wireless communication device, smart card, sensor module, wearable device, display device, or electronic package.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an “object of the invention” and “one aspect of the invention” section for a method of producing an antenna substrate by coating a photosensitive paste on an insulating substrate, patterning antenna/wiring/electrode regions, and curing them.
counterfactuals.output:
## Object of the Invention

An object of the invention is to provide a method of producing an antenna substrate in which an antenna pattern, wiring pattern, and/or electrode pattern can be formed on an insulating substrate with high positional accuracy and excellent productivity.

Another object of the invention is to provide a method of producing an antenna substrate capable of reducing the number of manufacturing steps as compared with methods using metal foil etching, plating, or screen printing, while enabling fine pattern formation suitable for compact or high-frequency antenna devices.

A further object of the invention is to provide a method of producing an antenna substrate in which a photosensitive paste is applied to an insulating substrate, selectively patterned by photolithography, and cured to form conductive regions, thereby improving pattern resolution, adhesion to the substrate, and manufacturing yield.

Still another object of the invention is to provide an antenna substrate production method that allows antenna regions, wiring regions, and electrode regions to be formed simultaneously or in a reduced number of process steps, thereby lowering production cost and improving reliability of electrical connection.

## One Aspect of the Invention

One aspect of the invention provides a method of producing an antenna substrate, the method comprising: coating a photosensitive paste on an insulating substrate; exposing the coated photosensitive paste to light through a photomask corresponding to at least one of an antenna region, a wiring region, and an electrode region; developing the exposed photosensitive paste to form a patterned paste layer defining the at least one of the antenna region, the wiring region, and the electrode region; and curing the patterned paste layer to form a conductive pattern on the insulating substrate.

In one embodiment, the photosensitive paste contains conductive particles and a photosensitive resin component. The conductive particles may include, for example, silver, copper, nickel, gold, carbon, or an alloy or mixture thereof. The insulating substrate may be a ceramic substrate, glass substrate, resin substrate, flexible film, or composite substrate.

In another embodiment, the antenna region, wiring region, and electrode region are patterned in a common coating layer of the photosensitive paste and are cured together, thereby forming an integrated conductive structure on the insulating substrate. The curing may include heating, photonic curing, ultraviolet curing, or a combination thereof.

According to this aspect, an antenna substrate having finely patterned conductive regions can be produced efficiently, with improved dimensional accuracy and reduced process complexity.

counterfactuals.output:
1. A method of forming an antenna substrate, comprising:  
   preparing an insulating substrate having a principal surface;  
   applying, by a coating method, a photosensitive conductive paste onto the principal surface, the photosensitive conductive paste comprising a conductive material and a photosensitive resin component;  
   drying the applied photosensitive conductive paste to form a photosensitive conductive layer;  
   selectively exposing the photosensitive conductive layer to actinic radiation through a photomask defining a wiring-line pattern and an electrode pattern;  
   developing the exposed photosensitive conductive layer to remove an unnecessary portion thereof and thereby form a patterned conductive paste layer including wiring lines and electrodes; and  
   firing or curing the patterned conductive paste layer to form conductive wiring lines and conductive electrodes on the insulating substrate,  
   wherein the wiring lines and the electrodes are formed with positional accuracy corresponding to the photomask pattern.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the conductive material comprises at least one of silver, copper, gold, nickel, aluminum, palladium, platinum, or an alloy thereof.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the photosensitive conductive paste comprises conductive particles dispersed in a photosensitive organic vehicle containing a photopolymerizable monomer, a photoinitiator, and a binder resin.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the coating method comprises screen coating, slit coating, spin coating, bar coating, doctor-blade coating, curtain coating, or roll coating.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein the wiring lines comprise antenna pattern portions configured to transmit or receive radio-frequency signals.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein the electrodes comprise connection electrodes configured for electrical connection to a semiconductor device, external terminal, matching circuit, feed line, or ground conductor.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the photomask defines the wiring-line pattern and the electrode pattern in a common exposure step, thereby aligning the wiring lines and the electrodes relative to one another without separate registration steps.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the developing step forms fine conductive patterns having a line width smaller than a minimum line width obtainable by directly printing a non-photosensitive conductive paste of comparable viscosity.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying step is performed at a temperature below a firing temperature of the conductive material so as to remove solvent while maintaining photosensitivity of the photosensitive conductive layer.

10. The method of claim 1, wherein the firing or curing step removes organic components of the photosensitive conductive paste and sinters or consolidates the conductive material to provide electrically conductive wiring lines and electrodes.

11. The method of claim 1, further comprising forming a dielectric layer, protective layer, solder resist layer, or insulating overcoat over at least a portion of the conductive wiring lines while leaving at least part of the electrodes exposed.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein the insulating substrate comprises glass, ceramic, glass-ceramic, resin, polyimide, liquid-crystal polymer, alumina, aluminum nitride, quartz, or a composite material.

13. The method of claim 1, wherein the antenna substrate is configured as an antenna module substrate, an RFID antenna substrate, a millimeter-wave antenna substrate, a patch antenna substrate, or a coil antenna substrate.

14. A method of manufacturing an antenna substrate, comprising:  
   coating an entire pattern-forming region of an insulating substrate with a photosensitive paste containing conductive particles;  
   patterning the coated photosensitive paste by photolithography to simultaneously define antenna wiring lines and connection electrodes; and  
   converting the patterned photosensitive paste into a conductive layer,  
   whereby the antenna wiring lines and the connection electrodes are accurately formed on the insulating substrate by a coating process rather than by direct printing of individual lines.

15. An antenna substrate manufactured by the method of claim 1, comprising:  
   an insulating substrate;  
   conductive wiring lines disposed on the insulating substrate and defining at least a portion of an antenna pattern; and  
   conductive electrodes disposed on the insulating substrate and electrically connected to the conductive wiring lines,  
   wherein the conductive wiring lines and the conductive electrodes comprise a fired or cured photosensitive conductive paste pattern formed by coating, exposure, development, and firing or curing.
